## Maturity estimation

Maturity offset and predicted age at peak height velocity (PHV) were computed with the moore2015 equations (primary) and the mirwald2002 equations (comparison). Inputs outside plausible ranges were rejected: age [[SPEC: 7.0, 20.0]] years, stature [[SPEC: 90.0, 210.0]] cm, sitting-height ratio [[SPEC: 0.45, 0.6]]. Status of the Mirwald girls coefficients: NOT yet verified against the original paper. TODO(human): verify all coefficients against the original papers.

## Growth twin

Stature was modelled per sex with a hierarchical SITAR-style model: a shared natural cubic spline mean curve with knots at [[SPEC: -6.0, -3.0, -1.5, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5, 3.0, 5.0]] years on the transformed age axis and per-athlete size, timing and intensity effects (intensity enabled: [[SPEC: yes]]). A per-athlete velocity deviation was included: [[SPEC: yes]]. The timing effect had a prior centred on the athlete's Moore estimate, with prior SD scale [[SPEC: 1.0]] years (learned: [[SPEC: yes]]; cohort-level offset learned: [[SPEC: yes]]; cohort timing prior: [[SPEC: no]]). Athlete effects were integrated out (size and velocity deviation analytically; timing on a grid of [[SPEC: 61]] points spanning [[SPEC: 4.0]] prior SDs either side; intensity on [[SPEC: 5]] points) and the shared parameters sampled with NUTS: [[SPEC: 4]] chains, [[SPEC: 750]] warm-up and [[SPEC: 750]] retained draws each, target acceptance [[SPEC: 0.9]]. [[SPEC: 200]] posterior draws were retained per athlete. Age at PHV was defined per draw as the age of maximum velocity of the athlete's fitted curve. Forecast horizon: [[SPEC: 90]] days.

## Movement screening and kinematics

Screening tasks were recorded with [[SPEC: 2]] smartphones (frontal, sagittal) at a minimum of [[SPEC: 60]] frames per second (target [[SPEC: 120]]). Tasks and detected events:

- drop vertical jump: events box drop, initial contact, peak knee flexion, take off, second landing
- single leg squat: events start, deepest point, return
- tuck jump: events not yet defined
- single leg hop distance: events take off, landing

Keypoints were estimated with mediapipe (tasks pose landmarker, model file pose_landmarker_heavy.task). Landmarks with confidence below [[SPEC: 0.5]] were removed; gaps of at most [[SPEC: 5]] frames were filled linearly and longer gaps left missing. Trajectories were low-pass filtered with a zero-lag Butterworth filter of effective order [[SPEC: 4]] and cut-off [[SPEC: 8.0]] Hz. Angular velocities were computed in degrees per second from frame timestamps. Joint angles: sagittal knee flexion, hip flexion, ankle dorsiflexion; frontal knee fppa, pelvic drop, trunk lateral lean. Knee flexion convention: 180 - included hip-knee-ankle angle; 0 deg = full extension. Foot contact was defined as foot height below [[SPEC: 0.06]] of leg length. Curves were time-normalised to [[SPEC: 101]] points. Between-limb asymmetry was computed from event- and window-level values only, as the symmetry angle. Trials with quality below [[SPEC: 0.6]] were excluded and logged.

## Agreement with marker-based motion capture (Paper A)

Agreement was summarised by bias, [[SPEC: 0.95]] limits of agreement, RMSE and intraclass correlations with [[SPEC: 0.95]] confidence intervals, stratified by maturity group (band [[SPEC: 1.0]] year) and sex. The pre-specified acceptance limit was RMSE below [[SPEC: 5.0]] degrees (provisional; TODO(human): confirm before analysis).

## Outcomes and athlete-week data

Outcomes were physiotherapist-diagnosed injuries in [[SPEC: 3]] groups (growth related, non contact soft tissue, all non contact), modelled separately; the primary outcome was growth related. For each athlete-week at risk, the outcome was an onset within the following [[SPEC: 4]] weeks. Weeks during time-loss and weeks whose outcome window was not fully observed were excluded. Predictors used only information dated before the prediction time. Exposure was summarised by weekly hours and an exponentially weighted average with half-life [[SPEC: 3.0]] weeks. Observed growth velocities used the latest [[SPEC: 3]] visits spanning at least [[SPEC: 60]] days.

Mechanistic load proxies (not validated against force plates: [[SPEC: yes]]) were defined up to a constant factor.

## Models

Confirmatory model: logistic regression whose predictors were taken, in this pre-specified order, from obs leg length velocity, twin maturity offset mean, mech patellar tendon load proxy bw, moore maturity offset, ewma hours, using only as many as the achieved numbers of athletes and events supported under the criteria of Riley et al. (at most [[SPEC: 5]]), one parameter per predictor. [[RESULT: number of predictors used and the athlete and event counts that determined it]]. All larger models below are exploratory.

Baselines (logistic regression):

- age only: age
- maturity growth velocity: moore maturity offset, obs height velocity, obs leg length velocity, obs mass velocity
- screening only: all columns with prefix `scr__`

Penalised hazard: elastic-net logistic regression with inverse penalty strength [[SPEC: 0.5]] and L1 ratio [[SPEC: 0.5]]; natural cubic splines with [[SPEC: 4]] knots for age, moore maturity offset, obs height velocity, obs leg length velocity. Boosted hazard: [[SPEC: 200]] trees of depth [[SPEC: 3]], learning rate [[SPEC: 0.05]], row subsampling [[SPEC: 0.8]]. These are starting values; TODO: tune in inner folds and report the tuned values.

Movement encoder: temporal CNN with [[SPEC: 4]] dilated residual blocks, [[SPEC: 32]] channels, kernel [[SPEC: 5]], embedding size [[SPEC: 16]]; graph variant with [[SPEC: 3]] blocks and temporal kernel [[SPEC: 9]]. The growth state conditioned the encoder by one of four modes (none, input concatenation, late fusion, FiLM). Encoders were pre-trained by masked-segment reconstruction (masked fraction [[SPEC: 0.2]], [[SPEC: 20]] epochs) with time-warping in [[SPEC: 0.9, 1.1]] and no left/right mirroring. Neural hazards were trained with learning rate [[SPEC: 0.001]], batch size [[SPEC: 256]], at most [[SPEC: 30]] epochs, early stopping after [[SPEC: 5]] epochs without improvement on [[SPEC: 0.2]] of training athletes, as ensembles of [[SPEC: 5]] networks. Growth uncertainty was propagated with [[SPEC: 30]] posterior draws.

## Validation and performance

All splits were grouped by athlete: [[SPEC: 5]] outer folds stratified by event status, [[SPEC: 3]] inner folds for tuning, and a temporal hold-out of the last [[SPEC: 0.25]] of follow-up. Preprocessing was fitted on training folds only. The primary metric was time dependent auc 4wk; also reported: pr auc, brier score, calibration intercept, calibration slope, ici, ece. Risk thresholds for sensitivity and specificity: none pre-specified yet (TODO(human): pre-register). Decision curves covered threshold probabilities [[SPEC: 0.005, 0.15]]. Confidence intervals ([[SPEC: 0.95]]) came from [[SPEC: 1000]] athlete-level bootstrap resamples. Subgroups: sex, maturity stratum, sport, age band, reported only with at least [[SPEC: 10]] events.
